messages:
sam-customer: Hey team — getting a bunch of 429s for the rwd-xl-64k variant after a campaign ramp. No code changes, just traffic surge :grimacing:

alice-support: Thanks — can you paste the exact error body and a repro curl? DM the API key.

sam-customer: DM sent. Error body looks like:
``
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_exceeded",
  "message": "per-model rate limit exceeded",
  "model": "rwd-xl-64k",
  "retry_after": 3
}
```
We see bursts: many requests succeed, then ~20s wave of 429s, then normal. We fan out ~40 parallel requests, ~30k context each.

mike-eng-sre: That pattern matches hitting per-model RPM/TPM + concurrency caps. 64k variants are token-heavy so TPM ramps fast. Are you sending as single calls or prefetching?

sam-customer: One-shot calls, about 20k prompt + ~5k generation expected per call.

lisa-support: Quick primer: limits are RPM (requests/min), TPM (tokens/min), and max concurrency. Big-context models consume more TPM and occupy slots longer, so concurrency and token-rate both matter. We also have a short burst window; sustained spikes get throttled to protect latency SLOs.

mike-eng-sre: Repro tip: throttle client concurrency to ~8-10 and implement exponential backoff with jitter on 429s. Also consider falling back to rwd-xl-16k or rwd-l-32k when you detect sustained 429s.

sam-customer: Any headers we can read to auto-adapt?

alice-support: We include headers when available: x-rw-ratelimit-limit, x-rw-ratelimit-remaining, and Retry-After (or retry-after). Note: in extreme overload some 429s may omit full headers, so still use conservative client limits.

sam-customer: Our curl used to repro:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-xl-64k","prompt":"<20k tokens>","max_tokens":5000}'
```

mike-eng-sre: We pulled traces for your tenant during the spike: token throughput spiked >3x and concurrency hit the model's soft limit. Runtime prioritizes active streams; new excess requests are rejected (429) if queueing would violate latency SLOs.

sam-customer: Can you share exact numbers for rwd-xl-64k (RPM/TPM/concurrency) so we map clients?

lisa-support: Can't post tenant quotas in-channel. PMing the published profile and your per-tenant caps. Short guidance: treat 64k as high-cost — reduce concurrency ~4x compared to 4k variants and cap token-rate aggressively.

mike-eng-sre: Also consider streaming: it lets you start consuming tokens earlier and abort if downstream backpressure appears, freeing server slots faster.

sam-customer: If we auto-fallback to rwd-xl-16k, is that routed automatically?

alice-support: For hosted tiers we recommend client-side fallback rules. Dedicated customers can opt into platform-side automatic fallback.

sam-customer: Need short-term mitigations — we have a campaign tonight.

mike-eng-sre: Short-term: spread the campaign over 30-60s, drop client concurrency, implement 429 backoff with jitter, and if possible reduce max_tokens to lower TPM.

deploy-bot: [deploy] autoscaler bump requested for tenant sam-customer — ticket #INC-8742 created.

sam-customer: Can you PM recommended client limits to start with?

lisa-support: PMing tailored suggestion now. Example starter limits: concurrency=8, sustained RPS=4, token-burst-budget=150000 TPM, enable streaming and aggressive 429/backoff. We'll send sample pseudocode.

mike-eng-sre: Quick backoff snippet you can use:
```
retry = 0
while retry < 6:
  resp = call_api()
  if resp.status != 429: break
  wait = min(2**retry, 30) + random_between(0,1)
  sleep(wait)
  retry += 1
```

alice-support: Follow-ups: infra is checking if we can temporarily raise burst headroom for your tenant tonight. If you capture request-ids for failing calls and share, we can trace exact queue decisions.

sam-customer: Will capture failing request ids and send. Appreciate the fast turnaround :pray: 

alice-support: Marking this open. Will update when infra confirms headroom. :thumbsup:
